title: Heavy Quarks Cast a Shadow
hook: A massive quark cannot radiate gluons straight ahead — it carves out a 'dead cone' around its own direction. CMS now sees that shadow in bottom-quark jets, disfavouring models without it at 4.3 sigma.
key_points: A quark shooting out of a collision sheds gluons, building up a jet of particles.
For a massive quark, collinear gluon emission is suppressed — the dead-cone effect.
It is the primary way quark mass shows up in a parton shower.
CMS analysed 59.8 inverse femtobarns of 13 TeV proton-proton data.
Bottom jets with transverse momenta of 40-200 GeV, from top quark pair production, were iteratively declustered.
The emission density versus subjet angle favours showers with the dead cone; models without it are disfavoured at 4.3 sigma.
content_html: When a quark is knocked out of a proton-proton collision it does not travel alone: it radiates gluons, which radiate further, until the whole cascade hadronises into a jet. For a light quark that radiation peaks at small angles to the quark's direction. Give the quark mass and that collinear radiation is choked off, leaving an emptier cone around its flight path — the dead-cone effect, and the clearest way quark mass shows up in a parton shower.
extra_html: The CMS collaboration measured it in bottom-quark jets, using 59.8 inverse femtobarns of 13 TeV proton-proton data. The trick is getting a clean sample and a clean observable: they take b jets with transverse momenta between 40 and 200 GeV produced in top quark pair production, then iteratively decluster each jet and measure the emission density as a function of the angular separation between the resulting subjets. Compared with the data, a Monte Carlo parton shower including the dead cone is favoured, while one without it is disfavoured at 4.3 standard deviations — evidence for an effect that has been in the theory for decades but is stubbornly hard to see directly.

related.title: Measuring the force that traps a quark inside the proton
related.hook: Nobody has ever seen a free quark. A sharpened reconstruction of the actual force tugging on one inside the proton comes out looking like a string pulled at constant tension.

related.title: Evidence for Sequential Υ(nS) Suppression in Light Ion Collisions
related.hook: Physicists just found the same 'melting pattern' that signals a quark-gluon plasma — the universe's primordial soup — in much smaller particle collisions than ever confirmed before.

related.title: What Actually Makes a Proton a Proton?
related.hook: Textbooks say a proton's identity lives in its three quarks. RHIC data hint it is really carried by a Y-shaped junction of the gluons tying them together.

related.title: The Standard Model
related.hook: Almost everything around you is built from a handful of particles obeying three forces — and one theory predicts it all with jaw-dropping precision, yet still can't explain gravity.

flashcards.back_html: A massive quark's gluon radiation is suppressed at small angles to its own direction, leaving a cone around its flight path that is comparatively empty of emissions.

flashcards.prompt: Why is the dead cone the headline signature of quark mass in a parton shower?

choices.text: Mass is what suppresses the collinear emissions a massless quark would produce freely
Only massive quarks produce jets at all
It changes the total number of quarks in the event

flashcards.explanation_html: Massless quarks radiate strongly at small angles. Giving the quark mass shuts that channel down, so the missing collinear radiation directly encodes the mass.

flashcards.prompt: How did CMS resolve the emission pattern inside a jet?
flashcards.back_html: By iteratively declustering the jet into subjets and measuring the emission density as a function of the angular separation between them.
